title: Modi and Trump meet at first Quad summit since 2024 as Beijing confirms Shenzhen big-three talks
dek: The four Quad leaders meet in Manila at 3.45 pm IST on Tuesday. Two days later Xi Jinping hosts Donald Trump and Vladimir Putin to discuss nuclear arms, Iran and Ukraine, with India not at the table.
author: Declaration Desk
body:
Prime Minister Narendra Modi is due to sit down with US President Donald Trump, Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi and Australian Prime Minister Anthony Albanese in Manila at 3.45 pm IST on Tuesday, for the first Quad leaders' summit since September 2024 and the first of Mr Trump's second term. Two days later, Chinese President Xi Jinping will host Mr Trump and Russian President Vladimir Putin in Shenzhen, a meeting Beijing formally confirmed on Monday.

The back-to-back meetings put India in an awkward spot. In Manila it sits at the table with the United States and its two closest Pacific allies; in Shenzhen, the leaders of the world's three largest nuclear powers will discuss arms control, the war with Iran and, at Moscow's urging, Ukraine, all issues that affect India directly, without India in the room. No separate meeting between Mr Modi and Mr Trump is planned in Manila, according to reports.

## What happened

The White House itinerary released on Monday put the Quad meeting at 6.15 pm Manila time, which is 3.45 pm IST, according to reports. Mr Modi is expected to fly back to New Delhi straight afterwards, reports said, citing unnamed Indian officials, who also said the agenda would cover protecting commercial shipping, critical minerals and the situation in West Asia, and that New Delhi expected modest outcomes. India holds the Quad's rotating chair, but the meeting is being held in the Philippines, which is not a member, on the sidelines of the summits it is hosting as chair of the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) this year.

Before the Quad, Mr Modi attends the 23rd ASEAN-India Summit and the 21st East Asia Summit on Tuesday. On Monday night he attended a dinner for visiting leaders hosted by Philippine President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. The ASEAN-India summit is expected to review the 2026-2030 plan of action under the two sides' Comprehensive Strategic Partnership; 2026 is the ASEAN-India Year of Maritime Cooperation.

In Beijing on Monday, China's foreign ministry spokesperson Mao Ning announced the Shenzhen meeting on 19 November. "This will be the first ever face-to-face meeting between the Chinese, Russian and U.S. heads of state," she told reporters, calling it "of groundbreaking significance". She said the three presidents would exchange views on "safeguarding world peace and enabling strategic stability", that details would be released "in a timely manner", and, asked about a separate Xi-Trump meeting, that "the two sides are in communication". She gave no agenda. The briefing did not mention India.

## What each side wants from Shenzhen

The three governments describe the meeting differently.

- Washington: White House spokeswoman Olivia Wales said Mr Trump would discuss the reduction of nuclear weapons, "whose proliferation President Trump believes is very dangerous". A White House official said Mr Trump would raise "the U.S.-Israeli war against Iran" but was not expected to raise Ukraine, according to reports.
- Moscow: Kremlin aide Yuri Ushakov said the talks would "continue the diplomatic efforts aimed at reaching a negotiated settlement" of the war in Ukraine, according to reports.
- Beijing: China has long said the United States and Russia, with far larger arsenals, should cut their own nuclear weapons before it joins arms-control talks. German President Frank-Walter Steinmeier said in an interview that when three-way talks on Ukraine came up in a recent meeting with Mr Xi, the Chinese leader showed "irritation" and "explicitly pointed out that this is a European conflict, in which the Europeans must also be at the table".

The US-China trade truce, which expires in January, is also expected to come up, reports said. Mr Trump is due in Shenzhen on Wednesday for the summit of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) forum, of which India is not a member.

## Background

The Quad (India, the United States, Japan and Australia) last met at leaders' level in Wilmington, Delaware, in September 2024. India was due to host the next summit in 2025, but it did not take place amid tensions with Washington over tariffs, including the additional 25% duty the United States imposed on Indian goods in August 2025 over India's purchases of Russian oil. The two governments announced a framework for an interim trade agreement in February, but no deal has been signed. A Modi-Trump bilateral meeting is now expected at the G20 summit in Florida next month, according to reports.

The Manila summits have taken place under the shadow of the South China Sea. At the ASEAN-China summit on Monday, Chinese Premier Li Qiang committed to an "effective, substantive and early conclusion" of a code of conduct for the sea, the Philippine foreign ministry said, according to reports, but set no deadline, after a 2026 target was missed. Mr Li, who represents Mr Xi at the ASEAN meetings, left Manila before the East Asia Summit, according to reports.

## What it means for India

The risks for India are concrete. A US-China-Russia understanding on nuclear weapons would be negotiated without India, which has a nuclear arsenal of its own and borders both China and a nuclear-armed Pakistan; China's position that it will not limit its arsenal until the US and Russia cut theirs leaves its build-up, which India's planners watch most closely, outside any deal. Any easing of US-China trade tensions could also shift supply chains that India has been trying to attract, while India still depends heavily on Chinese electronics components, pharmaceutical ingredients, solar equipment and rare earths.

The Iran war matters to India most immediately: shipping through the Strait of Hormuz, through which much of India's oil and gas imports normally pass, has almost stopped, and Brent crude was trading at about $92 a barrel on Tuesday morning. Protecting commercial shipping is on the Quad agenda for that reason. For India, the Quad is the main forum in which it works with Washington, Tokyo and Canberra on maritime security in the Indian Ocean and on alternatives to Chinese supplies of critical minerals; a summit with modest results, followed two days later by a three-way great-power meeting in China, would underline how much of the agenda is being set elsewhere.

Beijing presents the Shenzhen meeting as a contribution to "world peace" and "strategic stability". It has consistently described the Quad as an exclusive bloc aimed at containing China, a description the four members reject; they say the grouping is about a free and open Indo-Pacific and is not directed at any country.

## What happens next

- Tuesday, 17 November: ASEAN-India Summit and East Asia Summit in Manila; Quad leaders' meeting at 3.45 pm IST
- Wednesday, 18 November: Mr Trump arrives in Shenzhen for APEC
- Thursday, 19 November: Xi-Trump meeting and the China-Russia-US summit in Shenzhen, according to reports
- December: G20 summit in Florida, where a Modi-Trump meeting is expected, according to reports
